turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, and I'd like to start with who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me. Owen found out on his phone in the middle of a class.
"You've heard my points." That isn't an answer, Hale. Was Owen heard before that zero went in, yes or no?
With respect, this is exactly what lawyers do. Make noise until the facts go away.
I'm writing that down. Facts don't go away, Hale; they come on paper, with dates, so put yours on the desk. What do you have?
Your son cheated, and you're teaching him that Mom can make it disappear.

My child never lies, and you're now calling me a liar too. That's the second thing I've written down in five minutes, and when we're done here I'm going to the principal's office. The zero comes off, Hale, unless you can show me something better than an accusation.
